name: PixiJS
role: GPU-accelerated 2D renderer (WebGPU and WebGL) for sprites, text and filters
summary: Fast 2D rendering engine with scene graph, sprites, graphics, text, masks and a filter pipeline, running on WebGPU or WebGL. Driven by its ticker or manual render calls; output is a canvas that can be captured or extracted to pixels. Its strength is throughput for many sprites and shader effects, with a large ecosystem. Current line is v8.
use_when: Thousands of sprites, particles or textured meshes at frame rate
Over Konva or Fabric.js when GPU filters and blend effects are needed
Over Three.js when the scene is flat 2D and needs no 3D camera
Rendering a scene from script and extracting pixels via the renderer
avoid_when: Small vector-first scenes with interaction: Konva
Procedural noise or flow-field sketches: p5.js
Editable objects with SVG round-trip: Fabric.js
notes: 2026-10-26: pixijs.com did not state a licence or headless/Node support; MIT is from the npm registry and ticker control was not verified.

assessment.rationale: GitHub release v8.22.0 on 2026-10-01; MIT per npm; v8 supports WebGPU and WebGL. Clear GPU niche versus the Canvas-based neighbours.

evidence.result: 90 alpha PNG frames at 1280x720, 30 fps via Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4 screenshot capture; shuffled equals sequential in recorded and reproduction runs; changing hashes; frame45 alpha min0 max1. Frames0,45,89 visually inspected.
evidence.scope: Manual WebGL Graphics geometry and time-derived transforms; alpha PNG capture on macOS arm64. Not WebGPU, sprites, filters, text, export APIs or throughput.
